text:
alex_m: Hey — hit a weird perf cliff on MI250 today. ROCm runtime is missing a fused-gemm kernel for seqlen=512 so requests are falling back to the polyfill path on the CPU, p95 shoots up.
lia: ugh, do you have a quick profile? p95 numbers?
alex_m: Minimal repro run attached inline:
```
$ /srv/bin/infer --model: redwood-3b --seqlen 512 --backend rocm --batch 4
p50: 115ms
p95: 420ms
notes: backend chosen: polyfill_cpu (fallback)
kernel_probe: miopen_fused_gemm_v1 -> not found
KV hits: 92% (but cold prefix concat cost visible)
```
cheng: polyfill_cpu for fused-gemm explains the massive regression. We normally hit a GPU fused kernel at seqlen<=256 but for 512 there are multiple op signatures and we probably never compiled the miopen variant for that op shape.
alex_m: Right — interestingly, the runtime probe logic only checks presence of the exact kernel name (+op attrs). If not found we do an opaque fallback, which doesn't attempt compatible kernels or tiling permutations. That's step-1 to soften this.
lia: Could we add an autotune probe at startup that enumerates available kernels and registers compatible alternatives? Even a cheap heuristic (transpose dims, tile 32->64) would reduce these gaps.
ops: note: this would change the startup cost, we should gate it behind a feature flag and run it in background after health check.
perf-bot: run/1748201234/profiler completed — regression detected: baseline p95=128ms, current p95=418ms, delta +225% :chart_with_upwards_trend:
cheng: Also observed KV cache interplay — when polyfill CPU path runs, we see a burst of KV invalidations (we reserialize tensors back to CPU), which magnifies latency on warm prefixes. So it's not just kernel slowness, it's movement between device memories.
alex_m: Repro snippet of the routing decision logic: 
```py
# simplified route selection
if kernel_exists(name): use(kernel)
else:
    if fallback_policy == 'opaque': use(polyfill_cpu)
    else: try_compatible_variants(name)
```
We currently default to opaque. Suggest change to: try_compatible_variants -> quantized_gpu_variant -> remote_gpu_pool -> polyfill_cpu.
lia: We should also consider sequence-length-aware routing: if seqlen>384 prefer kernels compiled with larger tile sizes or route to dedicated pool with MI250-optimized builds.
cheng: +1. We can maintain a tiny catalog mapping (model, seqlen_range) -> preferred kernel families. Autotuner writes small JSON to disk and runtime reads it before in-process routing.
ops: ops concern: what if autoprobe reports availability that later disappears (driver update)? Need a periodic re-probe and clear on GPU reattach.
perf-bot: note: added trace link -> ci/artifacts/1748201234/rocm-probe-trace.txt (internal).

alex_m: Action items I can pick up:
- add compatible-variant lookup in routing (cheap)
- implement background kernel probe + catalog write
- add metric for "device-migration events" when tensors move between CPU/GPU (to quantify KV impact)

lia: I'll prototype a tiny autotune catalog schema:
```json
{
  "model_regex": "redwood-.*",
  "seqlen_buckets": [
    {"min":0, "max":256, "preferred_kernels":["fused_gemm_v2"]},
    {"min":257, "max":1024, "preferred_kernels":["fused_gemm_bigtile","tiling_v2"]}
  ]
}
```
cheng: For rollout, flag off by default, enable for internal dedicated clusters first. We should also add a nightly job that runs the probe matrix across active driver versions.
ops: I'll add a short ops doc with the feature-flag and fallback kill-switch. Also we need alerts for sudden increase in "device-migration events".
alex_m: ok i'll open a PR with the routing change + unit tests for kernel matching. Will paste a link here once created.
lia: thanks. if someone from runtime wants to pair on the probe heuristics ping me.

cheng: small note: let's avoid making the catalog too greedy — first iteration should prefer matching ABI names and only suggest tiling changes when there's no exact match. Keep it conservative.
perf-bot: TODOs recorded: #probe-catalog #route-fallback #metric-device-migrate

alex_m: end — will update thread after PR. :thumbsup:
